Rival orderings are excluded outright: grouping by ascending IPIP-BFM-50 item number gives alphas 0.50/0.57/0.33/0.42/0.31 and grouping in 4-item blocks gives 0.41/0.37/0.26/0.42/0.25, against the published 0.66-0.87. Keying (route 6) is confirmed item by item from the raw correlation matrix: within every trait the two items the form keys alike correlate positively (E +0.73/+0.63, A +0.31/+0.57, C +0.55/+0.74, ES +0.53/+0.52, I +0.29/+0.37) and every cross-keyed pair correlates negatively (range -0.64..-0.24), i.e. 20/20 items sit in the polarity class the form predicts; absolute direction is anchored by the paper's own reported signs (age x extraversion +0.221 vs published +0.23, age x conscientiousness +0.199 vs +0.20, age x neuroticism -0.185 vs -0.18) and by women scoring above men on agreeableness (3.66 vs 3.42) and conscientiousness (3.40 vs 3.02), which the paper states. TWO THINGS THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH. (a) It does not distinguish the two same-trait, same-polarity items in each of ten pairs (IPIP1/11, 6/16, 2/12, 7/17, 3/13, 8/18, 4/14, 9/19, 5/15, 10/20); those swaps leave every number above unchanged, and an attempt to break them with Topolewska et al.'s published per-item discrimination indices agreed on only 6 of 9 non-tied pairs, i.e. at chance. Hence PARTIAL.
